answer.answerText:
**No.** A fan’s electrical disconnect does not satisfy the required emergency manual ventilation control. MC § 405.2 requires each air-distribution system to have at least one manual control, at an approved location, to stop its supply, return, and exhaust fan(s) in an emergency—and expressly states: A disconnect switch shall not be considered a manual control. MC § 606.5 applies that same requirement to manual fan controls.

A separate manual emergency-stop control is therefore required; fan-mounted disconnects alone are insufficient. This answers only the manual-control requirement. If the system is a recirculating-air system subject to MC § 606.4.2, separate automatic fan-shutdown requirements may also apply.

answer.answerText:
**No.** A DOB permit exemption under AC § 28-105.4 does not eliminate independently applicable filings or approvals. The section expressly says that an exemption does not authorize work that violates the Code, Zoning Resolution, or other laws or DOB-enforced rules, and shall not relieve any owner of the obligation to comply with the requirements of or file with other city agencies (AC § 28-105.4).

Thus, the exemption is limited to the DOB permit requirement for the qualifying work; the applicant/owner must still determine and satisfy applicable requirements of other City agencies. AC § 28-105.4 does not itself identify which particular city, state, or federal agency approvals apply to a given project, so it cannot support assuming that state or federal approvals are unnecessary. For example, the supplied Code separately confirms that a DOB permit or approval does not relieve applicable New York State Department of Environmental Conservation permitting obligations for the specified deep soil/foundation work (BC § 3304.3.4).
answer.conclusion: **No.** A DOB permit exemption under AC § 28-105.4 does not eliminate independently applicable filings or approvals. The section expressly says that an exemption does not authorize work that violates the Code, Zoning Resolution, or other laws or DOB-enforced rules, and shall not relieve any owner of the obligation to comply with the requirements of or file with other city agencies (AC § 28-105.4).

**No—on the stated premise that four drinking fountains are required, four bottle-filling stations with no drinking fountains are not permitted.** Only up to 50 percent of the required fountains may be substituted: **2 of 4**. At least two drinking fountains conforming to PC § 410.1 must remain, and each substituted dedicated fixture must have a faucet for a container at least 10 inches high and be adjacent to or readily visible from a conforming fountain. Bottled-water dispensers cannot substitute. (PC § 410.3)

The remaining required fountains must each have both a drinking bubbler and a separate container-filling faucet; they also must meet the specified ASME/CSA, NSF 61 Section 9, ICC A117.1, and PC § 605 lead requirements applicable to drinking fountains. (PC § 410.1) The different rule for a restaurant where water is served is that drinking fountains are not required, but that exception does not change the stated premise that this building requires four. Likewise, the 15-or-fewer occupant-load exemption does not change that premise. (PC §§ 410.2, 410.3)

403.5 403.5 Drinking fountain location. Drinking fountains shall not be required to be located in individual tenant spaces provided that public drinking fountains are located on each story within a distance of travel of 500 feet (152 m) of the most remote location in the tenant space on such story. Where the tenant space is in a covered or open mall, such distance shall not exceed 300 feet (91 m). Drinking fountains shall be located on an accessible route. Section PC 404: Accessible Plumbing Facilities

1109.5.2 1109.5.2 More than the minimum number. Where more than the minimum number of drinking fountains specified in Section 1109.5.1 is provided, 50 percent of the total number of drinking fountains provided shall comply with the requirements for people who use a wheelchair and 50 percent of the total number of drinking fountains provided shall comply with the requirements for standing persons. Exceptions: 1. Where 50 percent of the drinking fountains yields a fraction, 50 percent shall be permitted to be rounded up or down, provided that the total number of drinking fountains complying with this section equals 100 percent of the drinking fountains. 2. Where drinking fountains are primarily for children's use, drinking fountains for people using wheelchairs shall be permitted to comply with the children's provisions in ICC A117.1 and drinking fountains for standing children shall be permitted to provide the spout at 30 inches (762 mm) minimum above the floor.

1109.5.1 1109.5.1 Minimum number. No fewer than two drinking fountains shall be provided. One drinking fountain shall comply with the requirements for people who use a wheelchair and one drinking fountain shall comply with the requirements for standing persons. Exceptions: 1. A single drinking fountain with two separate spouts that complies with the requirements for people who use a wheelchair and standing persons shall be permitted to be substituted for two separate drinking fountains. 2. Where drinking fountains are primarily for children's use, drinking fountains for people using wheelchairs shall be permitted to comply with the children's provisions in ICC A117.1 and drinking fountains for standing children shall be permitted to provide the spout at 30 inches (762 mm) minimum above the floor.

1106.8 1106.8 Electrical vehicle charging stations. Electrical vehicle charging stations shall comply with Sections 1106.8.1 through 1106.8.5. Exception: Electrical vehicle charging stations intended for use by a designated vehicle or driver shall not be required to comply with this section.

ACCESSIBLE. A site, building, facility or portion thereof that complies with Chapter 11 . ACCESSIBLE ROUTE. A continuous, unobstructed path that complies with Chapter 11 . CELL. See Section 408.1.1. FOOD COURT. See Section 402.2. NURSING HOMES . See Section 308 . 2 . 2 . OCCUPANT LOAD . The number of persons for which the means of egress of a building or portion thereof is designed . SERVICES. Includes, but is not limited to, toilet rooms, drinking fountains, public telephones and food. SITE. A parcel of land bounded by a lot line or a designated portion of a public right-of-way.

403.1.1 403.1.1 Fixture calculations. To determine the occupant load of each sex, the total occupant load shall be divided in half. To determine the required number of fixtures, the fixture ratio or ratios for each fixture type shall be applied to the occupant load of each sex in accordance with Table 403.1 . Fractional numbers resulting from applying the fixture ratios of Table 403.1 shall be rounded up to the next whole number. For calculations involving multiple occupancies, such fractional numbers for each occupancy shall first be summed and then rounded up to the next whole number. Fixture calculations in Group B office occupancies shall utilize the total occupant load on a given floor to determine the number of fixtures required for that floor. Exception: The total occupant load shall not be required to be divided in half where approved statistical data indicates a distribution of the sexes of other than 50 percent of each sex.

403.2 403.2 Separate facilities. Where plumbing fixtures are required, separate facilities shall be provided for each sex. Exceptions: 1. Separate facilities shall not be required for dwelling units and sleeping units. 2. In structures or tenant spaces where combined employee and public toilet facilities are provided in accordance with Section 403.3, separate facilities shall not be required where the total number of employees, customers, patrons and visitors is 30 or fewer. 3. In structures or tenant spaces where required toilet facilities for only employee use are provided in accordance with Section 403.3, separate facilities shall not be required where the total number of employees is 30 or fewer. 4. In structures or tenant spaces where required toilet facilities for only public use are provided in accordance with Section 403.3, separate facilities shall not be required where the total number of customers, patrons and visitors is 30 or fewer.

403.2.1 403.2.1 Family or assisted-use toilet facilities serving as separate facilities. Where a building or tenant space requires a separate toilet facility for each sex and each toilet facility is required to have only one water closet, two-family* or assisted-use toilet facilities shall be permitted to serve as the required separate facilities. Family or assisted-use toilet facilities shall not be required to be identified for exclusive use by either sex as required by Section 403.4. (Am. L.L. 2023/077, 6/11/2023, eff. 6/11/2023) Editor's note: For related unconsolidated provisions, see Appendix A at L.L. 2023/077 . * Editor's note: As set forth in L.L. 2023/077; intended reference is likelty "two family or assisted-use toilet facilities...."

1106.8.1 1106.8.1 Number of accessible vehicle charging stations. Where provided for common use, at least five percent of the total number of electrical vehicle charging stations per facility, but not less than one for each type of electric vehicle charging station, shall be accessible. Where a multiport electric vehicle charging station can simultaneously charge more than one vehicle, the number of electric vehicle charging stations shall be counted as the number of electric vehicles that can be simultaneously charged. The number of accessible vehicle charging stations are in addition to the required accessible parking spaces.

1106.8.5 1106.8.5 Electrical vehicle charging station controls. Electric vehicle charging stations and electric vehicle charging station controls shall comply with Sections 309.2 and 309.3 of ICC A117.1. Section BC 1107: Dwelling Units and Sleeping Units

1106.8.2 1106.8.2 Electric vehicle charging space. At each electrical vehicle charging station required to be accessible, the charging space shall comply with the requirements for a van accessible parking space complying with Sections 502.2 through 502.5 of ICC A117.1.

content.text:
- **No.** An exemption from a DOB permit under AC § 28-105.4 does not authorize work that violates the Building Code, Zoning Resolution, or other laws or rules enforced by DOB. ([nyc.gov](https://www.nyc.gov/site/buildings/property-or-business-owner/project-requirements-owner-outdoor-pool.page?utm_source=openai))

- AC § 28-105.4 expressly states that the exemption does **not relieve the owner of complying with requirements of, or filing with, other City agencies**. ([nyc.gov](https://www.nyc.gov/site/buildings/property-or-business-owner/project-requirements-owner-outdoor-pool.page?utm_source=openai))

- The DOB’s current “Do I Need a Permit?” guidance likewise states that exempt work remains subject to other laws and rules and that owners must comply with other City-agency requirements. This is guidance, not an independent enactment. ([nyc.gov](https://www.nyc.gov/site/buildings/property-or-business-owner/do-i-need-a-permit.page?utm_source=openai))

- The supplied **DOB NOW: Build Release Notes** provide concrete examples: certain DOB filings require LPC approval, FDNY approval, or DEC jurisdictional determinations and permits before DOB approval or permit issuance. Thus, a DOB permit exemption should not be treated as eliminating an independent agency filing or approval requirement. ([nyc.gov](https://www.nyc.gov/assets/buildings/pdf/dob_now_build_release_notes.pdf))

- The supplied **DOB NOW Application User Guide** was opened, but it did not provide a substantive rule resolving the general question; it is an application-procedure guide rather than the controlling legal authority. ([nyc.gov](https://www.nyc.gov/assets/buildings/pdf/dob_now_application_user_guide.pdf))

- **Scope limitation:** These sources do not establish which particular city, state, or federal approvals apply to a specific project. That determination must be made under the requirements of the other authority with jurisdiction.
